summary: Describes unknown key-share attacks against the use of DTLS-SRTP, and against the identity bindings used in WebRTC and SIP identity. In such attacks one party can be tricked about who it is really sharing keys with. The document explains the attacks and suggests mitigations. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Imagine you whisper a secret code to a friend, but a trickster makes your friend believe the code came from someone else. This document explains such mix-ups in secure calls and how to stop them.

questions: what is an unknown key share attack
how to protect dtls-srtp from identity attacks
